resources.string: Swoop is a keyboard. Android only uses it after you switch it on and choose it. Your old keyboard stays installed, so you can always go back.
Chosen right now: no (another keyboard is in use)

If the buttons do not open the right screen on your tablet: Settings > System > Languages and input > On-screen keyboard > Manage keyboards, switch Swoop on; then tap in any text box and use the keyboard icon at the bottom right (or the notification Choose input method) to pick Swoop.
To go back at any time: tap the keyboard icon (or the Choose input method notification) while typing and pick your old keyboard.
slide over the letters to type a word

Glide each word that is shown, with this keyboard, the way you do when you write. It takes about three minutes. Only these glides are kept (the path of your finger and the words the keyboard offered): nothing you type anywhere else, and nothing is learned from them. Then save the file and attach it to the chat, so the keyboard can be tuned to your tablet.
The first word was right %1$d of %2$d times (%3$d%%); the right word was among the first three %4$d times.
The first word was wrong for: %1$s (asked for → typed).
Next: save the file and attach it to the chat (do not paste it: it holds your finger paths).
One plain-text file in your Downloads folder.

A longer Glide practice. You glide whole paragraphs one word at a time, and short lists of words that look alike (the / there, for / or / our ...), each one several times. Glide the highlighted word with this keyboard the way you do when you write; if it types another word, just carry on. About 400 glides, 10 to 20 minutes, and you can stop after any page. Only these glides are kept (the path of your finger and the words the keyboard offered): nothing you type anywhere else.
The keyboard learns from my glides here
Every glide teaches it where your thumb lands, how you draw that word and which word it mistook it for. The words themselves are not counted as your own writing. Switch off to only measure.
Optional. Words you want extra practice on, separated by spaces: they get a page of their own, each one four times.
Word %1$d of %2$d on this page · %3$d glides so far
The first word was right %1$d of %2$d times (%3$d%%); the right word was among the first three %4$d times.
Altogether the first word was right %1$d of %2$d times (%3$d%%); the right word was among the first three %4$d times.
The keyboard did not learn from these glides (the switch was off).
The next page repeats the words that went wrong, together with the words the keyboard typed for them.

Type your e-mail addresses once. They show above the keys in every e-mail box, and when you type the start of an address yourself the keyboard offers the rest, with outlook.com, gmail.com and proton.me after the @. They stay on this device.
None yet. Addresses you type by hand in any box are added by themselves (never one you paste).
That does not look like an e-mail address.
Type a word. If the keyboard knows it, you can remove it so it is never suggested or glided again. If it does not, you can add it, and it is suggested when you glide its pattern.
Type a word or the start of one
None. A long press on a suggested word above the keys removes it too.
Only letters a to z can be added or removed.
\u201C%1$s\u201D removed. It will not be suggested again.
Translating is on: type in English, press Enter to turn it into Mexican Spanish, press Enter again to send.
Translating switched itself off because you left that box. Tap the translate key to turn it on again.
Translating is not available in this box.
Things you copy show up here. Tap one to paste it. Pin one to keep it: the rest is removed after an hour.
Clipboard history is off. Turn it on and the keyboard keeps what you copy while it is open.
Full size. Tap to make the keyboard full width again.
keyboard is still starting - glide again
Glide typing (slide over the letters to type a word)

It lives only on this device. Export writes ONE plain-text file into Downloads (it lists words you typed: keep it private, never paste it anywhere). Import adds a file to what is learned, including the file the Kestrel browser exported.
The keyboard is not ready yet. Try again in a moment.
. It lists words you typed: keep it private.

The file holds %1$s.\n\nIt is added to what this keyboard has learned. What is learned here stays; importing the same file again changes nothing.
The file could not be imported.
